objective: Determine whether the confirmed unauthenticated ippd crash is reachable after a factory-default boot or can be activated by an unauthenticated network request.

activation_trace.positive_path: libcms_core.so:rcl_ippCfgObject writes /var/printers.ini and sends CMS_MSG_START_APP for EID 45; the genuine smd positive-control run resolves EID 45 and launches /bin/ippd with that argument.
activation_trace.remaining_hardware_question: A physical USB-printer enumeration test can establish normal feature activation, but would still leave the finding dependent on attached/configured printer state.

always_on_pivot.supporting_dynamic_evidence: The byte-identical RAXE290 V1.0.9.82 web components were exercised with malformed HTTP framing, oversized headers and targets, public/setup routes, and malformed DNS inputs. The tested services remained available. SOAP parser reachability was incomplete in emulation.

current_firmware_validation.advisory_mapping: The June 2026 NETGEAR advisory maps RAXE300 V1.0.10.72 to CVE-2026-9211, an unauthenticated router-control issue. The following CVE-2026-3088 DoS entry lists Orbi products, not RAXE300.

package_retrieval.result: HTTP 403 from the official downloads namespace for every tested name; no public package was acquired.

current_firmware_validation.strongest_fixed_boundary_comparison: RAX30 V1.0.10.94 is the sibling fixed boundary for the same CVE-2026-9211 advisory and retains the byte-identical vulnerable ippd.
current_firmware_validation.conclusion: The public fixed-version boundary does not identify ippd as the patched component. Direct RAXE300 V1.0.10.72 binary comparison remains pending an OTA image from an owned router or public release.

classification.confirmed: Unauthenticated service-level memory-corruption DoS when dynamic IPP printing is active.
